A few days ago I described the sky from my place.  I very much appreciate your kind replies.

But there's more...

Just after I left the Orion and  his posse, Jupiter and Mars made an almost simultaneous appearance in the eastern sky.  For the next few days, they will appear as close to one another in the sky as they're going to be this year.  

They're an eerie, imposing, unearthly pair.  Jupiter is just old Jupiter--imperious, disdainful of the minor planets (which are all the rest), considers the sun its peer in this solar system.  

Mars lurks.  Grima Wormtongue comes to mind.  It is much dimmer.  Its rust color is emphasized, I think, by the nearby bright white of Jupiter. 

I stare and stare, and I cannot make my mind believe the brighter Jupiter is farther away than the dimmer Mars.

They make an interesting, maybe disturbing pair to see on a dark night.

I'd not be surprised if they're up to no good.

If CHAW—a dialectal variant of “chew” which is itself an abbreviation for “chewing tobacco” which is itself outmoded and nearly extinct—is your 1A, you have already established the kind of asinine puzzle you’re about to solve.

I know there’s a lot of discourse about what crosswords ought to be, and most of it is subjective.  But I think one of the foundational corners of it is that they should rely more on clever wordplay than pub trivia.

Knowing that LITHUANIA celebrates Stork Day, or that SCOOTER PIE is named after a baseball player is not clever or challenging in a meaningful way. You either know those things or you don’t, and when the crosses are equally full of trivia and nonsense words like SCHMOS (no “e”???) it becomes an exercise in frustration.
